intro: Searching for Invisalign near you usually means you want straighter teeth without fixed braces, and you'd rather deal with a practice you can actually get to. Invisalign is a brand of clear aligner that straightens teeth with a series of removable trays, planned digitally. We can introduce you to a private dentist who provides Invisalign, and they'll quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for Invisalign nearby usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search have a specific reason for wanting clear aligners and want to find a local practice that offers them.
needs: You've been self-conscious about crooked or gapped teeth and want a less noticeable option than metal braces.
You had braces years ago and your teeth have drifted, so you're looking at aligners to tidy them up again.
You want a dentist close to home or work because aligner treatment means regular visits over the course of your plan.
You're weighing up clear aligners against other options and want a professional to look at your teeth and explain what would suit you.
You've seen Invisalign advertised and want to know whether your own teeth are suitable before committing to anything.
context_heading: What to understand about Invisalign before you choose a practice
context: Invisalign trays are removable, so they only work if you wear them most of the day, every day, and take them out to eat and clean your teeth. Your dentist plans the movement digitally and will usually see you at intervals to check progress, with refinements if your teeth don't move exactly as planned. Retainers afterwards are what keep the result, so factor that into your thinking from the start.

Dentists, dental hygienists, dental therapists and dental nurses must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the GDC register online. Only people on a GDC specialist list can call themselves an orthodontist, so if a practice uses that title, it's worth checking. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales it's Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Say where you are and how far you're willing to travel, since you searched for Invisalign near you.
Describe what you'd like to change about your teeth, such as crowding, gaps or teeth that have shifted since braces.
Mention whether you've had orthodontic treatment before and how long ago.
Note any dental work you already have, such as crowns, veneers or bridges, as this can affect suitability.
Say whether you have a current dentist or haven't been seen for a while.
Mention any gum problems, jaw pain or other health conditions your dentist should know about.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the dentist you speak to
questions: Are you registered with the General Dental Council, and is the practice registered with the relevant regulator?
Will you be planning and supervising my Invisalign treatment yourself, or will someone else be involved?
Based on my teeth, am I a suitable candidate for clear aligners, and what alternatives would you suggest?
How many hours a day will I need to wear the trays, and what happens if I fall short?
What does the quote include, and are refinements and retainers part of it or charged separately?
What happens if something goes wrong or I'm unhappy with the result?

faqs.a: No. Clear aligners work well for many people, but complex bite problems or heavily restored teeth may need a different approach. A dentist needs to examine your teeth and discuss your options before you commit.

faqs.q: Do I need to wear the trays all the time?
faqs.a: Aligners must be worn most of the day to move teeth as planned, and you take them out to eat and clean your teeth. If you don't wear them enough, treatment can stall or the result may not be what was planned.

faqs.q: What happens after my Invisalign treatment finishes?
faqs.a: You'll usually need retainers to keep your teeth in their new position, because teeth can drift back over time. Ask how retainers are provided and whether they're included in your quote.

faqs.q: How do I check a dentist is properly registered?
faqs.a: You can check the General Dental Council's online register for any dentist, hygienist, therapist or nurse. If a practice calls someone an orthodontist, you can also check that they're on a GDC specialist list.
